flagged.evidence: It says that for every tuple of the other coordinates, the polynomial "vanishes at the m distinct points" in the first-coordinate interval. The chosen polynomial is only known to vanish at the previously selected evaluation points; the proof has not assumed it vanishes on the box. The root bound therefore does not apply as written. Add the short supposition that it vanishes throughout the cone, derive that it is identically zero, and contradict its choice.

The page says the argument proves the q^{2ν} Gram eigenvalue lower bound "for separated sites." The scoped lemma states the uniform bound with c=c(d,ν,a) only when 0<q≤1. For two Matérn sites at distance 2q, λ_min=1−k(2q)≤1, so a fixed positive c cannot give λ_min≥c q^{2ν} for arbitrarily large q. The summary omits this essential restriction.
